evidence.note: Read many spec files (ssr, headers-cookies, routes, navigation, advanced) to understand test expectations before/while implementing — input to verification design.

Ran full run_tests.sh ~24 times as the primary correctness oracle, but never obtained actual pass/fail counts (results file never produced); used it as a coarse all-or-nothing gate rather than a targeted debugger.

Stood up fixture apps manually in /tmp and ran `vinext dev -p PORT` to reproduce and debug dev-server startup failures, using errors to guide fixes — fixture-level verification, but confined to 'does it boot' rather than behavior.
Built a 'PIPE simulation' probe to reproduce the stderr pipe-buffer deadlock the test runner triggers — a real targeted probe, still at the infrastructure layer.

Ended by re-running the full suite and self-declaring completeness from a feature checklist; never ran targeted subsets, never curled manual servers to verify SSR/SSG/action output, never tested the production build/start path.

reasoning: The agent went beyond a pure code-only assumption and beyond a bare oracle: it read specs, stood up individual fixtures manually, and devised targeted infrastructure probes (dev-server boot tests, PIPE-deadlock simulation), using failures to drive fixes (above anchor 3). But it never ran targeted test subsets, its behavioral verification never advanced past 'server starts / basic HTML' (no HTTP probes of SSR/SSG/action output), the suite never actually reported pass/fail to guide it, and the production build/start paths were never verified — all required for anchor 5. This places it at a 4, between the oracle-only and subset-driven anchors.
